subject: Running a latent growth model with covariates

messages.author: 147a9a8a92ff12c4
messages.subject: Running a latent growth model with covariates
parts:
I am currently running a LGM with covariates and have some problems.

The study has six time points measuring the questionnaire scores, time-varying covariates (TVC) and time-invariant covariates (TIC).
I have now made 3 models. One LGM with no covariate, one with TVC and one with TIC.

1. Can I include the baseline measure as a time-invariant covariate? (Could I put the first time point as both the measured variable and the covariate)? If so, do I do it normally (regress the intercept and growth on the baseline measure) or is there anything special that I need to do? Because when I do it like a regular TIC, the output just became nonsense, with abnormally high intercept and growth.

2. I wanted to put both time-varying covariate and time-invariant covariate in the same model. I've tried to merge the commands of LGM with TVC and LGM with TIC, but I failed to do so and it showed:
     Error in lav_samplestats_icov(COV = cov[[g]], ridge = ridge.eps, x.idx = x.idx[[g]],  : 
     lavaan ERROR: sample covariance matrix is not positive-definite

May I know are there related examples or literature? I couldn't find any. Thank you all!

messages.subject: Re: Running a latent growth model with covariates
parts:
FYI: Here's my R script.

#LGM Model
model <- "
#measurement model
intercept =~ 1*TP1 + 1*TP2 + 1*TP3 + 1*TP4 + 1*TP5 +1*TP6
growth =~ 0*TP1 + (-1)*TP2 + start(-2)*TP3 + start(-3)*TP4 + start(-4)*TP5 +start(-5)*TP6
#time-invariant covariates
intercept ~ TIC
growth ~ TIC
#time-varying covariates
TP1 ~ TVC1
TP2 ~ TVC2
TP3 ~ TVC3
TP4 ~ TVC4
TP5 ~ TVC5
TP6 ~ TVC6
#variances and covariances
intercept ~~ intercept
growth ~~ growth
intercept ~~ growth
TVC1 ~~ TVC1 + TVC2 + TVC3 + TVC4 + TVC5 + TVC6 + growth
TVC2 ~~ TVC2 + TVC3 + TVC4 + TVC5 + TVC6 + growth
TVC3 ~~ TVC3 + TVC4 + TVC5 + TVC6 + growth
TVC4 ~~ TVC4 + TVC5 + TVC6 + growth
TVC5 ~~ TVC5 + TVC6 + growth
TVC6 ~~ TVC6 + growth
#error variances
TP1 ~~ TP1
TP2 ~~ TP2
TP3 ~~ TP3
TP4 ~~ TP4
TP5 ~~ TP5
TP6 ~~ TP6 
TIC ~~ TIC 
#factor means
TP1 + TP2 + TP3 + TP4 + TP5 + TP6 ~ 0*1 
intercept ~ 1 
growth ~ 1 
TVC1 + TVC2 + TVC3 + TVC4 + TVC5 + TVC6 ~ 1 
TIC ~ 1 
" 

#test model
fit <- lavaan(model, data=dataset)
summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Running a latent growth model with covariates
parts: 1. Can I include the baseline measure as a time-invariant covariate? (Could I put the first time point as both the measured variable and the covariate)?
Do one or the other.  It does not make sense for a baseline measurement to both predict a latent growth factor and be its indicator (outcome).

do I do it normally (regress the intercept and growth on the baseline measure) or is there anything special that I need to do? Because when I do it like a regular TIC, the output just became nonsense, with abnormally high intercept and growth.

Sounds like you should mean-center the baseline measure, so that the intercepts of the growth factors (let's call them Initial Status and Rate-of-Change to avoid confusion) are the averages for people with the mean at baseline.  If 0 is an extreme (or out-of-bounds) value for the baseline measurement, then the intercepts of growth factors will not apply to anyone meaningful in your sample.
2. I wanted to put both time-varying covariate and time-invariant covariate in the same model. I've tried to merge the commands of LGM with TVC and LGM with TIC
I don't know what "commands" you are talking about.  You just add parameters to model syntax.  The example on the ?growth help page includes both TVCs (c1-c4) and TICs (x1-x2).
May I know are there related examples or literature? I couldn't find any.

Have you read longitudinal SEM or related books, such as Jason Newsom's book or Grimm, Ram, & Estabrook?  The latter covers MLMs as well as SEMs.  They both have example R syntax.
